subject.title: Feature: browser upload tool fallback for non-standard file inputs (ByteUploader)

question: Should Browser upload gain an explicit custom-uploader file injection mode, and if so should it be DataTransfer drop, clipboard paste, native CDP drag, or a narrower supported subset?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses a local-file-to-page boundary outside the standard file input path, so automation cannot choose a silent fallback or permanent API shape without maintainer security and product intent.

options.title: Explicit custom-uploader mode
options.body: Add a separately named drop/paste/drag upload mode with managed-path validation, visible docs, tests, and live custom-uploader proof before enabling it.

options.title: Keep current upload only
options.body: Decline the custom uploader behavior for now and document that browser upload targets standard file chooser/input flows only.

options.title: External plugin experiment first
options.body: Ask for a ClawHub or local Browser-adjacent plugin experiment to prove the API and security model before core Browser plugin adoption.

recommendation.title: Explicit custom-uploader mode
recommendation.body: Add a separately named drop/paste/drag upload mode with managed-path validation, visible docs, tests, and live custom-uploader proof before enabling it.

likelyOwner.reason: The current Browser upload route and helper history most strongly points to steipete for the Browser plugin boundary and security-sensitive API decision.
